claim.why_it_matters: The required-word underline is the load-bearing notation in every general format, and this file's own convention for it is <u>...</u> - the immediately neighbouring one-word formats use '<u>REQUIRED</u>' (line 21402) and '<u>SECURE</u>' (line 21545). verdict.reasoning:
Independently confirmed on both sides, and the claim's quotes and line numbers are all exact.

PDF SIDE - rendered page 507 at 300 dpi (E:/Temp/specrecon/v507/spec_p507.png, printed folio 477) and cropped/upscaled the 13.18.48.2 General format region. The printed glyphs are 'REVERSE-VIDEO' with a single solid horizontal rule running the full width of the word, from the left stem of the 'R' to past the final 'O'. It is a continuous underline, not a hyphen artifact, not a table rule, and not an underscore character - it sits below the baseline and spans the entire token including the embedded hyphen. That is ISO's required-word notation, identical in weight and placement to the rule printed under REQUIRED (p506) and SECURE (p510).

MARKDOWN SIDE - specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 21445 is literally the 15 bytes '`REVERSE-VIDEO`' (verified with cat -A: no trailing whitespace, an inline code span, nothing else on the line). Lines 21443-21449 confirm the surrounding structure: the '### 13.18.48.2 General format' heading, a blank line, the backticked token, a blank line, then the 13.18.48.3 anchor. No <u> tag anywhere on the line.

RULED OUT THE STANDARD REFUTATIONS. The text is not missing or reflowed - the token itself is present and correctly spelled. It is not page-break furniture, wrapping, or hyphenation. It is not a case where the transcription simply chose a different but equivalent house style, because the file demonstrably has TWO established conventions for the required-word marker and line 21445 uses NEITHER:
  (a) Inline single-line formats use <u>...</u>. There are 16 standalone '<u>WORD</u>' general-format lines in the file, and within clause 13.18 alone every comparable one-word clause format uses it: AUTO (17368), BASED (17447), BELL (17489), BLINK (17597), FULL (18680), HIGHLIGHT (18889), LOWLIGHT (19396), REQUIRED (21402), SECURE (21545), UNDERLINE (22329).
  (b) Multi-line box-drawing formats are put in a ``` fence (which cannot carry HTML) and are COMPENSATED by an immediately following '> **Figure notes ...**' blockquote that names which words are underlined in the printed standard - e.g. 13.18.4.2 BACKGROUND-COLOR at 17403-17408 and 13.18.29.2 GROUP-USAGE at 18822-18827.
Line 21445 is an inline code span with no <u> and, verified by scanning lines 21444-21452, no figure-notes blockquote either. The required-word marker is therefore genuinely absent from the transcription with no compensating annotation. A mechanical harvest of required words from <u> tags silently misses REVERSE-VIDEO.

Severity 'cosmetic' is the right call: the format is a single word, so a reader still infers that the word is required, and no syntax or semantics is misrepresented. The loss is notational and tooling-facing, not meaning-changing.
verdict.corrected_description:
CONFIRMED as claimed, with two additions the claim did not mention.

FIRST - the file has a documented fallback for cases where <u> cannot be used: fenced format blocks are followed by a '> **Figure notes ...**' blockquote that states which words are underlined in the printed standard (see 13.18.4.2 at line 17408 and 13.18.29.2 at line 18827). Line 21445 has neither the <u> tag nor a figure note, so the omission is not covered by any existing convention in the file.

SECOND - this is a PATTERN, not a one-off. The complete set of standalone single-word general-format lines rendered as bare inline code spans instead of <u>...</u> is exactly three, and the fix should sweep all of them in one change set:
  - specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 7155  - `EXCEPTION-OBJECT` (8.4.3.6.2 General format)
  - specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 21445 - `REVERSE-VIDEO`   (13.18.48.2 General format)  <- the claimed instance
  - specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 26154 - `COMMIT`          (14.9.7.2 General forms)
Each should become <u>WORD</u> to match the 16 sibling lines already using that form.

Separately observed while surveying (NOT part of this finding, logged only so it is not lost): line 17321 'ANY LENGTH' (13.18.2.2 General format) carries no underline markup at all on either word.
